correctness.rationale: The source supplies oddness, squarefreeness, M odd, M>=3, and the strict ratio M<phi(n)/S_2(n). Reducing the exact squarefree equation modulo 3 gives an exhaustive three-pattern classification. The ratio factor (p-1)/(p-2) decreases with p, so the finite prime products are genuine maxima for a fixed factor count. The packaged verifier generates the primes by sieve and proves all critical inequalities by exact integer cross-multiplication.

originality.rationale: Hasanalizade 2022 proves only omega(n)>=7. Mandal 2025 is the decisive later comparison: it proves omega(n)>=17 generally and, for M=3, the all-2-mod-3 residue structure with omega(n)>=48. Full-text inspection shows no 2859 bound or exact admissible-prime product threshold. The present result extends the residue analysis to all multiplier patterns and computes the exact first product crossing at s_2859=56087. Exact-number, title, residue-pattern, and semantic searches found no covering statement.
residual_risks: An unindexed or private computation may already have evaluated the exact admissible-prime product cutoff.
Congruences beyond modulo 3 may force a substantially larger lower bound.

value.rationale: The number of prime factors of a hypothetical counterexample is a central invariant in this Lehmer-type problem, and both dedicated papers explicitly improve it. The new bound 2859 raises the published general lower bound 17 by more than two orders of magnitude and simultaneously raises the D_3 bound 48. The cutoff is natural: it is the exact first crossing of the extremal admissible-prime product, not an arbitrary search limit.
